name: Pioneer Valley
state_or_region: Massachusetts (Connecticut River valley — Mt. Tom, Holyoke Range, Northampton, Amherst, Mt. Sugarloaf & Mt. Toby)
agency: MA DCR, Mass Audubon, Kestrel Land Trust, USGS 3DEP & OpenStreetMap Contributors
summary: Traprock ridges above the Connecticut River: the cliffs of Mt. Tom, the Holyoke Range traverse from Mt. Holyoke's Summit House to Norwottuck and the Horse Caves, and north past Northampton and Amherst to Mt. Sugarloaf and the Mt. Toby fire tower, linked by the New England Trail and the Robert Frost Trail.

pois.name: Mount Tom
pois.note: Highest point of the Mt. Tom Range (1,202 ft); basalt cliffs above the Connecticut River

pois.name: Goat Peak Lookout
pois.note: Observation tower on the Metacomet-Monadnock Trail; hawk-watching in autumn

pois.name: Lake Bray
pois.note: Mt. Tom State Reservation, Route 5 entrance: parking, fishing pond and trail access

pois.name: Mount Holyoke
pois.note: Skinner State Park; the historic Summit House looks over the Oxbow (935 ft)

pois.name: Summit House
pois.note: 1851 summit hotel, now a museum (seasonal); summit road open in season

pois.name: Mount Norwottuck
pois.note: Highest peak of the Holyoke Range (1,106 ft)

pois.name: Horse Caves
pois.note: Overhanging ledges below Norwottuck, said to have hidden Shays' Rebellion horses

pois.name: Bare Mountain
pois.note: Short, steep climb from the Notch with wide views north over Amherst

pois.name: Notch Visitor Center
pois.note: Holyoke Range State Park, Route 116: parking, restrooms and trail maps

pois.name: Arcadia Wildlife Sanctuary
pois.note: Mass Audubon sanctuary on the Oxbow marshes (fee for non-members)

pois.name: Look Park
pois.note: Northampton city park on the Mill River

pois.name: Mount Sugarloaf
pois.note: Mount Sugarloaf State Reservation: sandstone cliffs and an observation tower over the river (652 ft)

pois.name: Mount Toby
pois.note: High point of the area (1,269 ft); fire tower on the summit, Robert Frost Trail

pois.name: Roaring Falls
pois.note: Cascades on Roaring Brook, Mt. Toby State Forest
